idiom_name: string-literal token union + Record<Token, parser> registry over record headers
implementation_notes: TypeScript's discriminated unions work on a payload property - the compiler narrows on a literal field inside the object - so the static-type story is content-based; the property-based realization keeps the token in the record header (kafkajs headers) and uses a Record<string, parser> or Map as the registry, then validates the parsed value. Because headers are not part of the static type, the token set is best expressed as a string-literal union and checked at the boundary; the compiler cannot narrow anything from a header for you.
pitfalls: Most clients type header values as string | string[] | undefined, so forgetting the array case makes the lookup fail while the code still looks correct.
Casting the parsed body (`as OrderCreated`) is not validation: the header states what the payload should be, not what it is - validate at the boundary when the producer is not fully trusted.

A header token narrows nothing at compile time, so type safety here has to be written by hand (a Token union plus a runtime check), unlike the payload-field discriminated unions the handbook describes.
